learning_objective: 🎯 [Kids will learn how to identify and use Adverbs to describe verbs, focusing on adverbs of manner (how) and adverbs of time (when).]
warm_up_hook: 🐢 How does a turtle walk? Slowly! 🐆 How does a cheetah run? Quickly! While adjectives describe nouns, we have a special group of words that describe actions. Let's meet the Adverbs!

lesson_modules.teaching_content: An Adverb is a word that tells us more about a Verb. It tells us HOW, WHEN, or WHERE an action is done. A very easy trick: many adverbs end in '-ly'!
examples_or_templates: The boy laughs [loudly]. (Loudly describes how he laughs)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: These adverbs tell us HOW an action happens. You usually make them by adding '-ly' to an adjective (like slow + ly = slowly).
These adverbs tell us WHEN an action happens. They don't usually end in '-ly', but they act like a calendar or a clock for your sentence!
examples_or_templates: I will go to the park [tomorrow].

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which word in this sentence is the Adverb? 'The dog barked loudly.'
❓ Which of these is an Adverb of Time (When)?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Change the adjective to an adverb by adding '-ly': 'The baby slept __________ (peaceful).'
subjective_practice.hint: Just stick '-ly' at the very end of the word!

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Underline the verb and circle the adverb: 'The deer ran swiftly.'
subjective_practice.hint: What is the action? And what word tells us HOW the action was done?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with an Adverb of Time (now, tomorrow, yesterday): 'I went to the zoo __________.'
subjective_practice.hint: The word 'went' means it already happened in the past.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🎭 The Action & Adverb Game
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write 5 actions (eat, walk, talk) on chits of paper, and 5 adverbs (quickly, slowly, angrily) on different chits. Draw one of each and act them out together (e.g., 'Eat slowly')!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Adverbs add more meaning to Verbs (action words).
⭐ Adverbs of Manner tell us HOW an action is done (e.g., quickly, softly).
⭐ Many adverbs are formed by adding '-ly' to adjectives.
⭐ Adverbs of Time tell us WHEN an action happens (e.g., today, soon, now).
